text: This place is awful. If there was a word more succinct than awful I would use it. Noxious pizza hellscape is an apt description.This place changes management all the time because the owners figure "it's a pizza place near a college campus, it'll be impossible to lose money." But let me tell you, when your service is as bad as Diamond Pizza you absolutely can. It's as if the owners of this place googled "how to run a pizza shop" and stopped reading halfway through the first result. Regularly, I'll order a couple cheese slices to go and wait for 10 to 15 minutes. On 4 or 5 separate occasions they've simply forgotten about my order, clueless as to why I've been standing in their store for the past quarter of an hour. It's not uncommon for the owners to lie directly to your face about when your order was put in the oven. Often times to even receive your food you'll have to call them out for lying. I can't even count on both hands the number of times I've been handed my food at Diamond Pizza with the words "we're really sorry about that" immediately following. These people are terrible. Literally every time I go to Diamond Pizza I have a bad experience. Sometimes its the rotating cast of 19 year old girls behind the counter texting and ignoring the line. Sometimes it's the $7 card minimum (conveniently $1 above the price of their lunch specials). The whole place reeks of attitude and ineptitude. One of the last times i was in there the woman behind the counter made me wait 10 minutes while she patronized a mentally handicapped man, speaking to him like a child about his headphones. I felt insulted for him and embarrassed for her. Often times I've seen "homemade" cookies in a bell jar near the counter. These are just Grandma's Cookies taken out of the wrapper, put on a napkin and up-charged by 100%. These people literally have no shame. So let's talk about their pizza. It's not good. Average is a complement. The cheese is runny, the sauce is weak and the crust is basic. If you're drunk or high it'll do the trick, but this certainly isn't up to the standards of even the most average Philly pizza. Pazzo's on Cecil B Moore just a few blocks south is far and above a much better pizzeria. Just the other day I ordered 3 plain slices to go and waited the standard 25 minutes. They were given to me in a box with paper places between each slice. The cheese stuck to each of the plates, so as i removed them all of the cheese on my slices was removed too. I waited 25 minutes for 3 slices that came to me already ruined. There was no need for the paper plates, they were already in a box. I've suggested instead of paper plates they use wax paper multiple times because wax paper would avoid the situation i just described. But I guess they didn't get that far in google searching yet. Don't go to Diamond Pizza. Tell your friends not to go to Diamond Pizza. Have your friends tell their friends not to go to Diamond Pizza.

I decided to get an estimate from Masselle's based on reviews online. Once I met Steve (the owner) I immediately felt like I was in good hands and decided to go with him for the repair. Steve was very courteous, sincere, and cared about me and my car. He was very sensitive to the timing of the repairs, and worked around my schedule to get the job done. When I picked up the car I was amazed with the work he did. The car looked like it rolled off the showroom floor as I could not tell any difference from when I bought it. Thank you Steve for being such a professional and putting me at ease through the whole process. I have never had to get body work done in my 24 years of driving and hopefully never will have to again, but if I ever did I would be back. Highly recommended!

I called the "worry no more" insurance contact and was informed this was a manufacturing defect and that we needed to deal directly with Macy's. So we have spent the rest of August with no living room furniture and had to cancel invitations we had extended to other guests since there is no place to sit. To add insult to injury Macy's sent me an email stating that if the representative cannot repair the pieces to manufacturers standards that I "may" have other steps I can take to return this cheaply made furniture- NEVER buy furniture from Macy's- They ate selling poorly made furniture and won't stand behind their products- I'll come back and update my review after this is resolved in September! text: "The Absolute Best Burger I've Ever Had!" My family and I visited Ulele, nestled within Tampa's newest park (Waterworks) on 22 February 2015. It was a quintessential, sunny and warm afternoon. This restaurant and brewery serve unique foods and spirits by fusing elements from a rich variety of Native American and multicultural influences, including those of European explorers. The menu features items indigenous to this area's waters and farms. We began our journey with the signature okra fries and Karson's Jalapeno Corn Beer Quick Bread. It was a good start to our inaugural experience. My partner and I enjoyed, based on our server's recommendation, the "Ulele Burger" while our daughter sampled the Fresh-roasted Yellowfin Tuna Salad. Folks, if you seek a quality, dining experience on a casual Sunday, take my advice and order the appetizers and Ulele Burger. You won't be disappointed. text: Virtually flawless. First of all, the place is beautiful. High ceilings, perfectly placed decor, and great acoustics. They did a fantastic job with the design. The people behind the counter were cool, outgoing, and seemed to enjoy working there. The latte I got was perfect, just the way I like it. If anyone thinks that pouring steamed milk over espresso does not take skill then they need to get that out of their head right now. It IS a learned skill and I appreciate anyone who can pull it off with that much finesse. For lunch I had the french dip. The baguette was fresh like it had been baked that morning and then kept at the perfect temperature until it was served. The steak was sliced thin and not over-done. The grilled onions were as sweet as they were plentiful. The cheese and the au jus tied everything together perfectly. I don't drink coffee while I eat so I got water from a self-serve fountain that similar to a beer tap. It had both still and sparkling water which I thought that was pretty clever. The rest of the menu looked great with a selection of other sandwiches, breakfast skillets, soups, salads, fine cheese, charcuterie and desserts. And let's not forget the bakery which was piled high with a wide variety of fresh bread and pastries. The ambience was great. Music-wise they played a lot of alternative rock like Belle & Sebastian, Vampire Weekend and the Pixies. The crowd had a nice mix of the families and couples grabbing lunch and enjoying each others company to the introverts who preferred to sit and drink sumatra by themselves for several hours. That the place attracts both is a sign of its quality and appeal. This really is the perfect gastro-coffee house, if that is a thing. I hope they take pride in this place because they nailed it.

text: I feel more strongly about this place than anywhere else in all of New Orleans. If you are going to create a business that sells a product as cheap and easy to make as a grilled cheese, you'd better goddamn make the best grilled cheese I've ever tasted in my life, where the flavors dance on my tongue and tingle my soul and it better at least attempt to be affordable. text: I'll provide the facts and you decide..... In December 2014 my wife and I were looking to have performed some much needed dental work. We have dental insurance and at that time I had a flexible medical savings plan with a certain amount I had saved to pay for dental care before the end of the calendar year. We first made sure that Cortaro Smiles was a "preferred provider" under the MetLife Dental plan. We made appointments to have a dental check-up and cleaning. They took dental x-rays in abundance, did an exam, had a dental hygienist look at our gums and stated both my wife and I needed dental planing (another dentist said planing wasn't needed) they did not clean our teeth but rather referred us their periodontist for additional costly procedures (the initial dental exam was $320 more than usual and customary for each of us and as I said it didn't include cleaning). In looking at our teeth they said we needed crowns and partial crowns. We asked for the cost on these services and this is where it gets confusing, I hadn't dealt with a dentist or doctor's office that operated this way, they "up-sell". They have a machine in the office that makes the crowns, and they gave us 4 options, the least expensive - purchase a crown from a lab (get a temporary, and wait for a week until it is manufactured), and then three different crown options that they manufacture, the cost on each option increases as the "warranty period" is extended (never have I had to think about purchasing a warranty on dental work in the past). We told the office billing person that we couldn't make a decision without knowing the cost. Initially she presented a very steep pricing estimate and after we told her we couldn't afford those prices she discounted their prices by 20% (given they were having a toys for tots drive at the time and we brought in two bags of presents) they then discounted the prices to the "usual and customary" amount the insurance company allows. She gave us a print out with all the services offered and in total separated the amounts by total billed, estimated insurance payment, and patient responsibility. We opted for the least expensive lab crowns but when we arrived on our appointments they told us they decided to provide the crown they produce for the same price. This dental work was completed the second week of December and we paid the "patient portion" by the first week in January. My wife also had some of the work she needed performed in February. We immediately paid the patient portion (outlined in the agreement) at the time she received services. As I needed receipts from the insurance company to bill my medical savings account for reimbursement, we had to contact the Dental office again and again asking them to bill. I called and talked to the insurance company and was told that Cortaro Smiles was submitting unsubstantiated bills that lacked the x-rays. After a few go-around's with the office they submitted the necessary paperwork and I had what I needed for reimbursement. Last week we received a note from a dental collection agency saying that we owed money (we never received a bill from the Dentist office, a phone call, an email... nothing). I created a spreadsheet utilizing the agreement we received from Cortaro Smiles and offsetting the amount my insurance company had paid. As it turned out they collected substantially more than the estimated dental insurance payments listed in the agreement. The analysis and their agreement demonstrate that we overpaid and were due a credit. This information was provided to their front desk staff and we were told it would be provided to their bookkeeper for review and they would perform an audit of the account. We met with Cortaro Smiles today and were told that the agreement they prepared and provided to us was not a contract and that they would not honor the details it provided. We were also told that we were lucky they didn't charge us their usual rates. We found this interesting as when a dental provider becomes a "preferred provider" they agree to receive payments based on a schedule of services, they are not allowed to charge more and are certainly not allowed to charge the patient the difference. I can tell you they billed our insurance for amounts that were significantly more than our agreement indicated and the insurance company of course reduced the eligible amounts back to what is allowed in the schedule. In the end we were told that what we owed and what we had overpaid was a wash and that we did not owe anything additional. I am in the process of informing my insurance company about our experience with Cortaro Smiles and we are preparing a detailed letter with supporting documentation to provide to the oversight entity for Tucson dental providers and are seeking legal counsel as well. *UPDATE* After speaking with a manager we did receive a refund for the overpayment. text: As Maegan P. explains it "My formula on this star count has everything to do with price vs. the food." I couldn't agree more. The bar was pretty cool too. I ordered the wedge salad and it was very good. It had a different spin than your regular wedge salad, using avocados, purple onions and tomatoes. For my entrée I ordered the braised short ribs with shrimp and grits. When the entrée came out I had to find my waitress to tell her that it was cold. Since I could not find her the bar manager got involved. I told him to just throw it in the microwave as it was getting late and I was hungry. He assured me that they were going to "re-fire it", but I am not sure what that meant. He and my waitress returned in less then a minute with a new plate and explained to me that this one had just been ordered by another customer but that I could have it instead of waiting on mine. He waited there until I tried it to make sure it was fine, but it was just as cold as the first one. Not to mention that I had to point out that it was missing the pimento cheese spread on top of the grits. The third time was the charm. Being in the south you figure they know how to do grits. The flavor was good but they were extremely salty. The shrimp needed a little more seasoning on the other hand. The braised short ribs were very tender but had zero flavor. They tasted just like boiled meat. For some reason the recipe includes fried shoestring potatoes on top. There is no better way to ruin a good piece of meat than to throw fried potatoes or onions on top of it. They should have used sautéed mushrooms in butter or caramelized onions on top to try and import some flavor to the meat. My waitress gave me a free dessert and the manager knocked off $10 from my entrée. This kind of took away some of the bad experience. But when you just got recognized on national television and had your restaurant renovated for free, and demand high prices for your food, you better make sure that the experience is well worth it. text: I have been going to the original Mel's since I was a child. They opened up a second location in Carrollwood many years ago, that was quite big, always seemed busy, but it was closed. As a customer of many years, I really appreciate the original Mel's on the North side of Busch Blvd. , between Busch Gardens & 22nd Street. When I walk in the door I just smile expectantly & patiently wait to place my order. I will not apologize for usually ordering the same dawg. A chili, cheese dog, squirting of mustard & diced raw onions & don't even think about forgetting my fries. The outside of the building is nothing, except a small converted house, with a parking lot. Inside it is remenencent of an old fashioned dinner, with soda shop tables & everything is primarily nostalgic. OMG, my order is up! I am like a kid making my way to get the food, my food...I think I might be drooling, well just a little. I sit at my table and dive right into, the hot, waiting food. The fries are crispy, crunchy, golden fried, yet soft and flaky inside......yummy so good. The dawg, I really think that maybe it should be eaten with a knife and fork, but where is the fun in that? I just pick up that beautiful, sexy dawg with both hands. It knows my name & is ever so quietly serenading me, I can't resist & take that first bite. The bun is soft & warm, the chili isn't very spicy, but full bodied and plenty of it, some of which comes tumbling out. The cheese is melted perfectly and the raw onions are chopped very fine. Yup, it's a classic, but certainly one that never goes out of style. From the soft bun, to the snap of the expertly cooked dawg, the hint of spicy mustard, hot Chili & cold chopped onions , all in the perfect ratio, it is all mine. After the first bite of the dawg, I can sit back and relax and enjoy the rest of my meal. My expectations have been met, as usual. I am dining with an old childhood friend & will continue to do so as long as Mel & I are in Tampa. What's a girl to do? Always appreciate and hold old friends close.

text: My fiancée, our 2-year-old daughter and I had a "student" salesperson come to our door last night (7pm - right after dinner, to be sure) looking to sell us educational books, posters and other materials. She was from Estonia and said she was visiting our city (Regina, SK, Canada) for the summer, selling these Southwestern Advantage books as her summer job. At 35, she seemed a little old to be studying business in university, but whatever, maybe she is a mature student. Anyway, her sales tactics applied a lot of pressure and a) prey on people "wanting the best for (their) kids" and b) require you to be a almost impolite in getting her to leave. Some obvious tactics included: - Showing us a binder full of "testimonials" from satisfied customers. They were handwritten on little cards, although they all seemed to be in the same handwriting (presumably the salesperson's). She referred to "Mike and Karen" in Grande Prairie, AB and "Ryan and Tammy" in White City, SK as though they were personal friends or it would make their statements more meaningful to us. They aren't and it didn't. - The cost for the full package of 20+ books and materials was a whopping $535. She rationalized a single 20-page hardcover book as costing $30 at a bookstore (I estimate it would be more like $6.99 actually), to emphasize the "savings" of buying the full package. The markup was pretty shocking, actually. She also made reference to a family that said "compared to the amount of money they spend on camping as a family, $535 wasn't a lot of money." Okayyy. - Presenting an option to pay in installments. I asked how they did that and she said "we trust you to pay over time," which I interpreted as giving buyers the books and accepting online payments via credit card. Um nope: She proceeded to show us post-dated cheques a previous buyer had given her. - Pumping our tires for being "good parents" because when she showed one of the entry-level books to our daughter, she immediately responded to the colors and animals on the pages, calling some of them out by name. "You obviously read to your daughter," she said. "Good job." - Repeatedly asking "what (we) like best" about the books, to reinforce their positive traits and inherent value. - Dismissing our offer to buy just a single entry-level book ("Sorry, they're only sold in packages of 5 or more") or to later purchase them ourselves online ("That would defeat the purpose of having students go door-to-door."). - Asking what might prevent us from buying her books (to which we answered: "We can take out books from the public library for free" and "There's no guarantee our daughter won't lose interest in Southwestern Advantage books, like she has with books we already own") and then having zero response for these valid arguments. - When we finally told her we weren't interested, she revealed perhaps her most discomforting tactic: Asking us to identify other homes on our street with young children. We pointed her toward two other houses, but immediately felt bad after doing it. So there you have it. I wasn't impressed by any of the above maneuvers and as I said, the whole business model of aggressively pushing overpriced books on young families stinks to the high heavens. I advise other young parents to not let these people into your home.

text: I think that the main problem I had with this place was that I came in with high expectations from other self-serve Mongolian BBQ places. Comparing this place to others, like Genghis Grill (which is now closed) is comparing night and day. Let me explain: The sauce selection is miserable, with little explanation as to the actual flavors. Your options of actual sauces are "Chef's sauce", teriyaki, Soy, and Chile, with options of cooking wine, sugar water, ginger in water, and garlic in water as other "sauces". Comparing this to other places is an issue, with others often having 2x the sauces, including descriptions as to the types of meat they go with best and a description of their flavors. They have the space for 2x the sauces by simply removing duplicates. The meats were the worst part, by far. The meats were frozen-solid, super thin slices that had little to no flavor or texture. I don't know how they could, given the meats come in almost-paper-thin slices. Chicken and beef end up tasting basically the same, and again, there's no marinade or real options on any of them. The "seafood" was an assorted seafood menagerie that looked honestly dangerous to eat. The texture of the cooked meats varied from powdery when cut across the grain to stringy when cut with. The vegetables also presented a problem, in particular with cooking them. I'm not sure if the issue is with the cooking process or the cooks themselves, but it seemed that meat was the main choosing factor for cooking time. Putting spinach and broccoli in my food was a mistake - the spinach came out so wilted that it seemed like small dark-green balls, while the broccoli was raw for the most part, and cold in others. This is just one example; my girlfriend's mushrooms also came out raw. I think offering better meats would likely alleviate this issue. The soups were another problem, but I can only review the egg flower soup - it was bad. Really bad. The crappiest hole-in-the-wall Chinese place will make better soup. Bland, flavorless, and boring. Lastly, the price was an issue. If you come in any time after 4:00 PM, you're immediately priced for All-you-can-eat, whether you want it or not. At 11.99 for an exponentially mediocre (bordering on bad) stir-fry bowl, this is a bad deal. If you go in on a low-carb diet and just want large amounts of vegetables and meat, I guess this isn't the worst option if you don't care about flavor or texture. It's just kind of ridiculous that no one tells you that it'll be all you can eat. The only sign we saw was on our second way through, and the sign was very small on the corner of the glass. There was another sign at our table, but it doesn't exactly help given you get seated after your food is paid for. If the food was really good, maybe 11.99 would be worth it, but no matter how much food I can get, I still don't think I'll ever go back here again unless they made a major change.

I purchased a pair of boots at this store and was actually quite happy with them, so I thought I'd do the ailing company a favor and post a nice review on their website. BIG mistake!! I received such a snarky email back from the corporate office! Why on earth do they bother offering the option to review products if they only publish the ones they like??? (Incidentally, I believe "manufacurte" in the quoted letter is supposed to be "manufacture.") I quote: "Your opinion is very important to us and the JCPenney community. We appreciate you taking the time to write a review on product. Unfortunately your review did not meet our guidelines for posting on our site. We cannot tolerate mention of country origin or manufacurte, and reviewers must maintain positive feedback to our business practices and products. We encourage you to review our guidelines and resubmit your better review on Arizona Brit Womens Ankle Boots. Thanks for being an active member of the JCPenney community. Sincerely, The JCPenney Team" End of quoted material. WTH??? I wrote a very positive review -- four stars, actually. I mentioned an inconvenient truth in my review -- the fact that it is getting very difficult to find items that are manufactured in the USA in JCPenney stores, and for this, they "cannot tolerate" my review? Very disappointing, and not just for the poor grammar and spelling. This company doesn't want feedback; they want free propaganda. They'd have been much better off not publishing my review and not sending me such a snotty letter -- this way, they lost a positive review AND a loyal customer.

text: Don't judge a book by it's cover! Or umm, I mean a restaurant by the fact that it used to be a Taco Bell? Little Korea is a family run restaurant that is filled with unique and tasty vittles. Not only that, but vittles that you'd be hard-pressed to find else where in New Orleans. Aside from a thriving Vietnamese community, most would say New Orleans definitely lacks diversity when it comes to other types of Asian Cuisines. And although we've really been stepping up the game over the past couple of years, I would still agree. Next time you're driving down S. Claiborne and are thinking about turning into one of the three fast food chains to your right, don't. Pull a left instead and pop into Little Korea. Upon walking inside you'll notice K-Pop music in the background, a Korean Soap Opera on the television, and probably a large group of extended family members catching up over some Korean BBQ. Sounds better than your original plan of trying to stuff your face with a crunch wrap supreme while driving now doesn't it? I don't know about you, but all I'm normally left with after that is a stomach ache, shame, and a giant nacho cheese stain on my shirt. Everyone that works there is super friendly and eager to teach people about Korean food. No reason to be afraid to ask for suggestions or to even substitute the skinny metal chopsticks for wooden ones. I've tried a couple of things at Little Korea, but I definitely have certain dishes that I crave and always come back to. If it's cold out, order the Spicy Tofu Stew. It's a fiery red soup served in a stone hot pot that is filled with silken tofu, pork, and has a whole egg cracked straight into it. I swear it can cure any cold or heat up any chilly New Orleans night. When it's hot out, I normally order the Spicy Cold Noodles. It's a bowl of cold buckwheat noodles with a spicy red sauce, thinly sliced brisket, pickled daikon, cucumber, and a hard boiled egg on top. Super refreshing and interesting when the temperature is in the mid 90's. Some of my other favorites include the Spicy Pork and Squid, Bulgogi, Kim Chi Fried Rice, Japchae, Dukbokki, and the Spicy Pork Bi Bim Bop. If you've never had Korean Food before The Bulgogi Bi Bim Bop is a great place to start. You really can't beat all that crispy rice! My favorite part about this place, however, is definitely the Banchan. Banchan are traditional Korean side dishes that change daily and come with any entree. I've had everything from Kimchi to Scallion Pancakes here and they never disappoint. Bottom line, give Little Korea a try. It's a quaint place packed with unique and funky flavors, you really can't go wrong.

She couldn't get my tire to drop from underneath the truck (I've had problems with this, so has my dad and even a tow truck guy before), so me being in Franklin, knew if I wanted to get a tire, I was going to have to pick her up and put the truck on a jack and bring the busted tire into NTB since they were the only ones open past 6pm on a Saturday. By the time I got the tire off, NTB would be closing in 10 minutes. It would take me 20mins to get there. I called and the gentlemen said there was no way they could stay later because they had plans. Now I understand why they said no (Valentines Day), but instead I had to leave the truck on a jack in Nashville over night and I got my tire taken care of someplace else the next day. I once had the same situation happen while I was in a truck with a different friend, it was the same situation, got the spare on the truck, found out the spare was no good, rolled the tire to Discount Tire down the street 10 mins before closing on a Saturday night, they switched out the tire stayed past closing because they didn't want 2 girls to be stranded on the side of the road in Murfreesboro TN. Good job NTB, yes we were stranded and yes, something that could of taken you 30 mins led me and my sister to spend her last day dealing with this. I had to get my financee who lived an 1hr 40mins away to us up, go home and help us out the next day... You would of gotten an awesome review and a hefty tip but instead my fiancee is making sure I give y'all an honest review. :(

On the recommendation of Miss Amy, I decided to go with one of the Signature Benedicts, the Crabcake Cavallo. It was a somewhat expensive yet worthy choice. The crab cakes were moist and tasty. My only complaint was that the two poached eggs were rather uneven in how much they were cooked. The yolk on one was almost the same as a hard-boiled egg and the other still orange but firm. I also did not really taste the Andouille infusion on the Hollandaise, but it was still quite tasty. Amy was very kind to us, taking great pains in making sure my daughter had everything to enjoy her pancake later. So often you get a to-go box and that's it; Amy made sure we had plastic ware, extra butter and syrup. Little touches like that make such a difference! text: I have been to River City Casino a few times before, but this was my first stay at RC Hotel. I booked a room for a Saturday night for $139. I wouldn't pay any more than that for a hotel room - especially at a casino. Remind you, the Hotel is only a few months old, but it is very clean. The distance from the parking garage to the Hotel and the distance from the room to the Casino floor are not as much of a walk as other Hotel/Casinos in St. Louis. I had dinner at 1904 and the food was good and priced appropriately. I played craps and blackjack from 9pm-3am and didn't lose money so naturally I was in a pleasant mood. After a number of $4-8 drinks, I slammed a late night burger from Burger Bros. I had a great night sleep in the King bed and checked out the next morning. For the room (with taxes), dinner and drinks, I spent about $220. The key is finding people who want to have fun gambling and play with them. Opportunities for Improvement: - Wait staff in the Casino took forever to bring drinks around. On a Saturday night, the supply of servers was inadequate for the demand of drink orders. - The shower water was bathtub warm at best. Maybe I should have taken a shower earlier than 10:30am though. - One of the dealers didn't move very fast and was kind of boring. Might be better to move those dealers to weekday AM shifts. For a table with $10 minimum bets, players expect more of an energetic "atmosphere". - No mini fridge in the room.
label: POS

text: Entering the restaurant you're greeted by a nice pink puffy fish, that's the money fish. You'll come back to him later and it's a great way to start and end your meal and they know that. The man who took our order I was really vibing with. He's the kind of man who finishes you're sentences, but you're not mad because he did a better job than you ever could. He got that half star back right away. Again they put him at the entrance/exit so you leave with a smile, all part of the plan. The atmosphere was definitely interesting. The restaurant is divided into a standard sit down and a "cobra bar and grill." We were lucky enough to get the cobra bar seating. There was a nice beat synced up with one of the tvs playing a Victoria's Secret model montage. Are they gonna play that the whole night you're wondering? Don't worry they'll change that later. I gotta say the beat was a little jarring at first, but soon enough you'll look down to see you're finger tapping and look back up to see the heads bobbing across from you. At the sports bar they were playing the clippers and spurs game. A man was sitting there the entirety of the time we were there. You could tell he was a regular by how well the employee and he were getting along. It's nice to see that kind of community outreach. Even though the game was out of reach for the clippers with 30 seconds left they were still talking and smiling like they still have a chance. You gotta love seeing optimism like that in a business. Just when you think isn't the Victoria's Secret modeling getting to be a bit much they switch to a live ac/dc show to bring it on home. Eatin noodles and rockin out to dirty deeds, doesn't get much better than that. I dont know what other programs they offer, your experience may vary. The food was good. We left. Said goodbye to the puffy fish and nice man, like they wanted, and called it a night. I was pleased with my evening. Final grade 4/5 stars. Where did that other star go you ask? Cmon I'm not giving 5 stars, don't be ridiculous.

text: Save your money! Nightfall is a total bust. I took my teenage stepdaughter to this "haunted town," thinking it might be good for a few scares. We weren't expecting much. And not much is exactly what we got. After paying $55 for both of us to get in, we finished the three main attractions (The Iron Door Mine, The Bunker, and Psychomania) within 45 minutes and realized we had just completely wasted our money. It was good we'd done them all early though, because the later it got, the longer the lines became. After completing the three haunted houses, we grudgingly shelled out another $10 ($5 per person) to go on a "haunted hay ride." The driver of our wagon was really fun, and the scares on this attraction were pretty good, too. Still, the extra $10 stung. The shows are good, but you have to arrive at least a half hour early for every show if you want decent seats. If everything was included in the entry fee, Nightfall would be an okay experience at almost $30 per person. If you wanted to complete all attractions, most of which cost an additional $5, then you would be looking at a cost of at least $60 per person. Nightfall is not worth this price AT ALL. I cannot stress this enough. Don't waste your money.

Now the vibe...and to say the biggest negative is the staff is to understate things. The "owners" seem interested only in making this their private little pub - outsiders NOT WELCOME. If obeisance is not paid expect to be treated rudely. Most of the patrons seem to keep their distance from them. The rest of the bar staff take their lead from these "owners" - if they are not there they are friendly and helpful, but once they appear their behavior changes. I would recommend avoiding Murphy's at all costs...unfortunately there are few bars within walking distance, so I occasionally stop in, have a beer, catch a game, and hope for these "owners" to move on to other opportunities and for Murphy's to be the true neighborhood bar it has the potential to become. text: Two things make this park stand out from the other Carmel parks: the gigantic silo-looking slide and the splash pad area. The slide is amazing, and so big that you can see it from 116th street as you're driving by. The splash pad has two shower-like nozzles that spray water, and the water then trickles down into a big wading area that is perfect to plop down little babies to splash in the calm water. Farther down the wading pool it gets a little deeper (like ankle-deep), but it's still the perfect setup to get wet and cool, but stay safe. Other things this park has: lots of swings, a tractor-themed play set, a rope climbing structure, and some tunnels that, at first glance look like water drainage pipes, but no -- kids can climb through them! (Well, my kid did. I'm almost positive that's what they're there for.) There's also a lake with a long dock where you can fish, a Little Free Library, an area with picnic benches ... there's so much here that I feel like I'm missing something!

text: Shaya fills a niche in the New Orleans culinary scene that many have set out to do, but few have been successful. As a vegetarian, it is difficult to find a restaurant where both I and my meat-eating friends are fully satisfied and satiated. Shaya on the other hand offers such an eclectic offering of food, that everyone always leaves happy. Of all of my experiences at Shaya, the ones that particularly stand out are when I have been able to have Maddie as our server. She knows the menu so well and is able to so clearly articulate the flavors of each and every dish. Maddie always lets us know her personal favorites, but is very quick to offer recommendations that comply with my personal dietary restrictions. The service is unparalleled and I can confidently say I will continue going to Shaya and requesting Maddie as my server for years to come.

Once inside it feels like you've entered into a world where friendliness and warmth is the new normal. It's a pretty big area that's a great place to go if you're looking to get some studying done, catch up with a friend, or just brighten up your day. text: I heard that Pumpkin among the top restaurants in Philadelphia and had super high expectations going in - the food definitely exceeded them! I was so pleased with my meal and will definitely be going back. Although the venue is small (make your reservations early), it does have a "classier" vibe, despite being a BYOB. The service is relatively slow... though it's definitely worth it considering the quality of food that you're receiving. I went for restaurant week this year, and the menu was nothing short of amazing. Started off the night with a Beet and Mozzarella appetizer (I forget the specific name), and the flavors and textures of the dish just meshed so well together. I loved pairing the tartness of the beets and dressing with the creaminess and lightness of the mozzarella. It was definitely a unique taste, but I loved it nonetheless. My friends all wound up getting a lamb pasta dish as their appetizer, and they did nothing but rave about it for the entire night. Now for the entree. The entree was by far my favorite part of the meal. I ordered the Rainbow Trout, and I can surely say that this trout was the best fish that I've ever had. It looked almost like salmon upon first glance, but the taste was so different and had a lighter and more delicate texture than salmon. I absolutely LOVED the char on the skin of the trout - I could eat it all day. Weirdly enough, the trout skin was probably the best part of the entire meal and made the entree dish. I highly, highly recommend getting any fish that is on their menu because with the way that Pumpkin chars the skin, it's simply perfection. To finish it off, I had an cake (I want to say almond financier?) topped with dates, apples, and a wonderful scoop of vanilla ice cream. It was an incredible dessert and just a great way to finish off the meal with a bang. The combinations of flavors was just delightful, and the dessert was rich but not overly rich. My friends all wound up getting the Chocolate Pot de Creme, which my friends thought was too sweet and decadent for their liking. Personally, I have a huge sweet tooth, so I thought that the dish tasted great, but I definitely do understand how the richness of the dish can be a little overwhelming. Overall, I loved my experience at Pumpkin, from the freshly baked bread at the beginning to the small bags of pumpkin seeds at the end of the meal. I highly recommend grabbing a nice bottle of wine and bringing your closest friends and loved ones here - it's great!

text: Added two stars for the views from the roof, the atmosphere and decor on the inside, and the fact that they have managed to restore a historic building that would likely have met the wrecking ball otherwise. But, boy, talk about over-hype and a place that is trying too hard to do something (I'm not sure what it's trying to do though, really). Minus three stars for terrible service, plastic cups for cocktails, and aggressive staff. Sat a half-consumed drink on an empty table to turn around and take a picture, had a staff member come up and take it. When I turn around and see them walking away, I ask for it back, he looks at me, says "Sorry, 5 second rule, gotta clear these tables," and throws it away. Prior to this, some angry bouncer accused my friends of stealing juice from the bar (the bartender looked very annoyed and confused when the bouncer, who claimed to be a manager, asked him to charge us two dollars, which he reluctantly did). Tried to complain to management, however this guy had the gall to follow me to the front and stand aside vehemently claiming his righteousness to his manager when I informed him of the issues. But, that was just my personal experience. My observations led me to believe that it was a very confusing place, with not much direction or idea of what it wanted to be. As previous reviewers have stated, the ordering system is not appropriate for what they're trying to do, especially on a busy day. I wish that I had a better experience, I wanted to go back. Unfortunately they need to fire some staff members, or instill in them a sense of customer service and aplomb. I also admit that it really wasn't my scene (way too frat-tastic), so I didn't have a great attitude after coming through the door.

text: Went here with my girlfriend last Friday morning. We were in a bit of hurry, as we had intended to go to Patachou (or something?) but couldn't find parking as a bunch of neckbeards were at GenCon. With 45min until my Megabus left and still no food, I decided to head to Milktooth. Thus, when we got there, we were in a hurry. I confirmed with the hostess that we could be in and out in 35min, and she said that would be no issue. We sat down at the bar to get food and coffee. It was a little slow to get our waters, but our waitress was nice when she got around to us. I got a cortado, girlfriend got a macchiato. My cortado was well-done, although the macchiato was small. We were in a rush to order, and our stress was multiplied by the stupid menu names (ie. things had hipster names that made it hard to discern what exactly we were ordering). I went with a BLT Dutch Baby and my girlfriend went with a fruit-covered Dutch Baby. She was later saddened to see that someone else had gotten an eggs benedict--what she had intended to get at the other restaurant but couldn't find here due to the menu. The food was definitely good. My partner really enjoyed her Dutch Baby. I liked the bacon and tomatoes of the BLT Dutch Baby, but I was a little thrown off by the shredded lettuce. I get that it might have been normcore, but with a shitton of arugula and spinach just sitting in the kitchen, why would you shred iceberg at a restaurant of this caliber? Paying was quick and easy, and it would have been reasonably priced had we forgone the espresso drinks. I look forward to giving Milktooth another try when I am not so rushed. It seems like a promising concept, and the atmosphere ticks all of my hipster buttons. (As a final note, I was surprised at just how many people they had working. Employees and customers were almost at a 1:1 ratio.)
label: NEG
